enzyme_name: Cytosolic carbonyl-reducing enzymes (aldo-keto reductases AKR1C1-AKR1C4 and carbonyl reductase 1) reducing oxcarbazepine to its 10-monohydroxy derivative (GP 47779 / licarbazepine)
organism_context: Human liver cytosol; oxcarbazepine is a prodrug whose active species is the 10-monohydroxy derivative
rationale: Ichida et al. quantified oxcarbazepine ketone reduction in human liver as essentially entirely cytosolic, partitioned among AKR1C1-4 and CBR1, each a single-domain NADPH-dependent carbonyl reductase. The broad substrate range of AKR1C enzymes (including hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity) is one oxidoreductase chemistry on many substrates, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: The enzymology runs ketone to alcohol (oxcarbazepine to GP 47779), so ModelSEED's '<' points backwards; the apparent near-equilibrium comes from NADPH having been abstracted to a bare 2 H+, and KEGG itself labels R08321 'unclear/incomplete'.

enzyme_name: Cytochrome P450 3A4 (unspecific monooxygenase, EC 1.14.14.1) performing the second N-demethylation of the methadone metabolite EDDP to EMDP
organism_context: Human liver and intestinal microsomes; CYP2B6/CYP2C19 contribute to the first methadone N-demethylation
rationale: KEGG annotates R08340 as CYP3A4 N-demethylation, and Moody et al. and Oda & Kharasch confirmed CYP3A4 catalyses the successive N-demethylations of methadone to EDDP and EMDP. CYP3A4 is a single heme-thiolate monooxygenase domain; its obligate partner NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase is a separate polypeptide, not a fused second activity.
direction_note: Written as a bare EDDP/EMDP isomerisation, but a CH2 unit (released as formaldehyde) plus O2 and NADPH are all absent; stripping the O2-consuming oxidation removes everything that makes this step one-way EDDP to EMDP.

enzyme_name: (-)-alpha-Bisabolol synthase (MrBBS), a class I sesquiterpene synthase (the ModelSEED label 'alpha-bisabolene synthase' is wrong for this product: cpd06515 levomenol is alpha-bisabolol, not bisabolene)
organism_context: Matricaria recutita (German chamomile); the same single-enzyme step is used in engineered yeast/E. coli alpha-bisabolol strains
rationale: Tai et al. characterised alpha-bisabolol synthase converting FPP directly to alpha-bisabolol; it is a single class I terpene-synthase alpha-domain with one Mg2+-dependent ionisation active site. Multiproduct behaviour in terpene synthases is substrate-cation promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Class I terpene synthases are made irreversible by diphosphate departure; ModelSEED's equation omits PPi entirely, which is why both estimators return a nonsensical ~+400 kJ/mol and force a '<' call.

enzyme_name: alpha-Humulene synthase (humulene cyclase), a class I sesquiterpene synthase cyclising FPP to alpha-humulene
organism_context: Zingiber zerumbet ZSS1 (first committed step of zerumbone biosynthesis); humulene-forming TPSs also known from Abies grandis and many angiosperms
rationale: Xu et al. characterised the zerumbone pathway sesquiterpene synthase that makes alpha-humulene from FPP, paired with a separate short-chain dehydrogenase; the synthase is a single class I terpene-synthase domain with one active site. No fused second catalytic activity is reported for humulene synthases.
direction_note: Diphosphate, the leaving group that makes the cyclisation irreversible, is missing from the equation, so the +440 kJ/mol dGPredictor value and the resulting '<' are artifacts.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG flags R08393 as a multi-step, incomplete conversion of geranyl diphosphate to nerol (plausibly neryl-diphosphate synthase plus a phosphatase, or geraniol synthase plus an isomerase)
rationale: KEGG's own COMMENT marks R08393 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction', so no single protein catalyses GPP to nerol as written and the enzyme cannot honestly be named. Using 'unknown' rather than guessing a monoterpene synthase.
direction_note: Net flux in planta runs prenyl diphosphate to monoterpene alcohol, pulled by phosphoanhydride cleavage, but the equation omits the diphosphate so the thermodynamics (~+420 kJ/mol) is meaningless.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG states R08394 is the sum of R08393 (GPP to nerol) and R08083 (nerol to neral, an NAD+-dependent geraniol/nerol dehydrogenase)
rationale: KEGG explicitly decomposes this entry into two separate enzymatic steps, so no single enzyme catalyses GPP to neral and no functionality call applies to one protein.
direction_note: Both constituent steps run biosynthetically toward neral; the '<' call comes from a ~+420 kJ/mol estimate produced by the missing diphosphate and missing NAD+ couple.

enzyme_name: (+)-3-Carene synthase, a class I monoterpene synthase cyclising geranyl diphosphate to car-3-ene
organism_context: Conifers (Picea abies, Pinus spp.) and some angiosperms; the gene family is the plant TPS-b/TPS-d monoterpene synthases
rationale: The enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry (GPP to car-3-ene is by definition a 3-carene synthase) rather than confirmed for this ModelSEED entry, which carries no name, EC or xref. Class I monoterpene synthases are single-active-site enzymes; multiproduct carene synthases are still one catalytic activity.
direction_note: The diphosphate leaving group that makes terpene cyclisation one-way is absent from the equation, so the +424 to +457 kJ/mol estimates and the '<' direction they imply are artifacts.

enzyme_name: Geraniol synthase (GES), a class I monoterpene synthase that ionises geranyl diphosphate and quenches the cation with water to give geraniol
organism_context: Catharanthus roseus (CrGES, first step of the iridoid/MIA pathway), Ocimum basilicum, Valeriana, Cymbopogon
rationale: GPP to geraniol is the defining single-enzyme reaction of geraniol synthase, a single class I TPS domain; this is a well-established monofunctional terpene synthase and is called largely from established knowledge plus the Christianson cyclase review.
direction_note: Both the water co-substrate and the diphosphate product are missing; with PPi release deleted the estimators see a ~+425 kJ/mol uphill step and vote '<', the opposite of the real one-way hydrolytic ionisation.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG flags R08397 as multi-step and incomplete (GPP to geraniol by a terpene synthase, then NAD(P)H-dependent double-bond reduction to citronellol by an ene-reductase/geraniol reductase)
rationale: KEGG's COMMENT marks this a multi-step, incomplete entry, so there is no single catalysing protein to classify; the chemistry requires at least a terpene synthase plus a separate reductase.
direction_note: Both constituent steps are biosynthetically one-way toward citronellol; the reductant and the diphosphate are both absent from the equation.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG states R08398 is the sum of R08396 (GPP to geraniol) and R03581 (geraniol to geranial, NAD+-dependent geraniol dehydrogenase)
rationale: KEGG itself decomposes the entry into two enzymatic steps, so no single enzyme catalyses GPP to geranial and no per-protein functionality call is possible.
direction_note: The hydrolytic ionisation of GPP and the NAD+ oxidation both run forward in planta; the missing PPi and NAD+ couple are what produce the spurious +417 to +428 kJ/mol and the '<' call.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG flags R08399 as multi-step and incomplete (GPP to geraniol/citronellol then oxidation to (R)-(+)-citronellal)
rationale: KEGG marks the entry multi-step and incomplete, so no single protein can be named or classified; at minimum a terpene synthase, a double-bond reductase and an alcohol dehydrogenase are involved.
direction_note: All constituent steps are biosynthetic toward citronellal; the diphosphate and both redox couples are missing from the equation.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; the ginkgolide pathway downstream of levopimaradiene runs through levopimaradiene hydroxylase (CYP720B-type) and several further, mostly uncharacterised cytochrome P450s
organism_context: Ginkgo biloba root bark and leaf
rationale: KEGG R08402 is flagged 'multi-step reaction' and spans the whole oxidative elaboration of levopimaradiene into ginkgolide A; only two of the required Ginkgo P450s have been functionally identified to date, so no single catalysing enzyme exists for this entry.
direction_note: ModelSEED has additionally mis-mapped the substrate: cpd03629 is copalyl diphosphate (KEGG C06089), whereas KEGG R08402 starts from levopimaradiene (C11879), and nine oxygens plus the lost diphosphate are unaccounted for, so no direction read from this equation is meaningful.

enzyme_name: Glycolate dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.99.14), the GlcD/GlcE/GlcF three-subunit FAD- and Fe-S-containing membrane-associated oxidase of the glc operon; GlcD is the FAD-linked catalytic subunit
organism_context: Escherichia coli glc operon (b2979/b4468/b4467); homologues throughout bacteria and in the plant/algal glycolate dehydrogenase
rationale: Pellicer et al. showed the E. coli glc locus encodes three separate subunits of glycolate oxidase/dehydrogenase; per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and the catalytic FAD subunit GlcD carries one activity, glycolate 2-oxidoreduction (it also accepts (R)-lactate, which is substrate breadth, not a second activity).
direction_note: IUBMB defines EC 1.1.99.14 with an unknown physiological acceptor; ModelSEED substitutes free FAD/FADH2 for the enzyme-bound FAD that passes electrons through Fe-S to the quinone pool, so the +15 kJ/mol 'reverse' call is the FAD couple's, not the real one. Physiologically the enzyme only oxidises glycolate to glyoxylate (it is how E. coli grows on glycolate), matching the LLM's forward call.

enzyme_name: Mg-protoporphyrin IX monomethyl ester oxidative cyclase: the anaerobic radical-SAM form BchE (which matches the H2O-dependent chemistry written here) or the aerobic di-iron form AcsF/ChlE/CRD1-CHL27 with its Ycf54 partner; this entry is only the first (13(1)-hydroxylation) of the cyclase's three successive oxidations
organism_context: Anoxygenic phototrophic proteobacteria (BchE), cyanobacteria, algae and plants (AcsF/CHL27; barley Xantha-l, maize ZmCRD1)
rationale: The cyclase performs three sequential oxidations of one bound substrate at a single active site (radical-SAM in BchE, di-iron in AcsF) rather than carrying several fused catalytic domains, so it is iteratively monofunctional; the aerobic enzyme's dependence on a separate Ycf54 subunit is a complex, not a fusion.
direction_note: Free NAD+/NADH stands in for the real oxidant (O2 for AcsF, or SAM plus reduced ferredoxin for BchE); chlorophyll biosynthesis flows one way toward the isocyclic E ring, so the forward direction is the physiological one and the dGPredictor-driven '<' is an artifact of the substituted couple.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; dolichotheline is N-isovalerylhistamine, so the chemistry requires histidine decarboxylation to histamine followed by isovaleryl-CoA-dependent N-acylation, and no enzyme of either step has been characterised in the producing cactus
organism_context: Dolichothele sphaerica / Mammillaria (Cactaceae) imidazole alkaloids
rationale: KEGG flags R08412 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction' and no enzyme has been cloned for dolichotheline biosynthesis; searches returned no enzymology, so 'unknown' is the honest call rather than inventing an acyltransferase.
direction_note: Free isovalerate stands in for isovaleryl-CoA and the CO2 lost in decarboxylation is absent, so the +99 to +137 kJ/mol used to call '<' is not the real step's free energy; biosynthetic flux runs toward dolichotheline.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; the conversion of L-pipecolate to 1-indolizidinone requires at least an oxidation/activation of pipecolate and an acetate-derived two-carbon extension plus cyclisation, with no characterised enzyme
organism_context: Indolizidine alkaloid-producing plants (Leguminosae/Convolvulaceae); pathway known only from classical feeding studies
rationale: KEGG marks R08415 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction', so no single enzyme catalyses it; no protein has been assigned to indolizidinone formation in the literature.
direction_note: The missing acetate/malonyl extender and the lost water make the +51 to +63 kJ/mol estimate meaningless; alkaloid biosynthesis flows away from pipecolate, not back to it.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; (-)-sedamine formation needs a cinnamoyl-CoA (not free cinnamate) condensation onto Delta-1-piperideine followed by side-chain trimming and ketone reduction, and no Sedum/Lobelia enzyme has been cloned
organism_context: Sedum acre / Lobelia piperidine alkaloids; pathway inferred from precursor feeding only
rationale: KEGG flags R08422 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction' and a literature search returned no characterised enzyme for sedamine biosynthesis, so no single protein can be classified.
direction_note: Free cinnamate replaces the activated cinnamoyl-CoA and the condensation water is absent, so the thermodynamics behind ModelSEED's '<' does not describe the real chemistry; flux runs toward the alkaloid.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; lobelanine assembly from Delta-1-piperideine plus two aryl-C3/aryl-C1 units is a polyketide-type multi-step condensation in Lobelia, with no enzyme characterised
organism_context: Lobelia inflata and relatives (Campanulaceae); pathway known only from feeding experiments
rationale: KEGG flags R08423 as a 'multi-step reaction' combining two separate acyl condensations onto piperideine; searches for Lobelia alkaloid enzymology returned nothing, so there is no single catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: Free cinnamate stands in for an activated thioester and the decarboxylations/waters are absent; lobelanine is the biosynthetic product, so the forward direction is the physiological one.

enzyme_name: Unidentified NAD(P)H-dependent ketoreductase that reduces one of the two side-chain ketones of lobelanine to give lobeline; KEGG labels the step only as 'oxidoreduction'
organism_context: Lobelia inflata; the reductase has never been purified or cloned
rationale: The chemistry is unambiguously a carbonyl reduction, but no Lobelia protein has been assigned to it, so the catalysing enzyme cannot be named and 'unknown' is the honest functionality call.
direction_note: The hydride donor is abstracted to a bare 2 H+, so eQuilibrator's tight +7.9 kJ/mol is the free energy of a pseudo-reaction, not of an NAD(P)H-coupled reduction; biosynthetically lobelanine is reduced to lobeline, which is the LLM's forward direction.

enzyme_name: A622, an NADPH-dependent PIP-family (isoflavone-reductase-like) reductase that reduces the nicotinate-derived pyridine ring in nicotine biosynthesis, working as a reductase/oxidase pair with the berberine-bridge-enzyme-like BBL
organism_context: Nicotiana tabacum / N. benthamiana root nicotine pathway
rationale: A622 is a single-domain NADPH reductase, but the 2026 in vitro reconstruction of the complete nicotine cascade shows the ring reduction acts on a cryptically glucosylated nicotinate rather than the free acid KEGG R08426 writes, so the enzyme assignment to this exact equation is weak; KEGG itself marks the entry 'incomplete'.
direction_note: The NADPH that drives the ring reduction is written as 2 H+ and the activating glucosylation that makes the reduction feasible is absent entirely, so the ~+10 to +20 kJ/mol behind ModelSEED's '<' is not this step's free energy; flux runs from nicotinate toward nicotine.

enzyme_name: None - KEGG states R08427 is a nonenzymatic decarboxylative condensation of 1-methylpyrrolinium with 4-(1-methyl-2-pyrrolidinyl)-3-oxobutanoate (the latter supplied by a type III polyketide synthase in the tropane/pyrrolidine pathway)
organism_context: Atropa belladonna / Solanaceae and Erythroxylum pyrrolidine alkaloid branch
rationale: KEGG's own COMMENT calls the step 'nonenzymatic decarboxylative condensation', so there is no catalysing protein to classify; Bedewitz et al. established the upstream PKS/P450 route that supplies the oxobutanoate substrate.
direction_note: The step is spontaneous and is pulled one way by CO2 release toward cuscohygrine - but ModelSEED's equation has dropped both the co-substrate and the CO2, leaving a bare 1-methylpyrrolinium/cuscohygrine pair whose +13 to +79 kJ/mol cannot support any direction call.

enzyme_name: Littorine synthase (LS), a serine carboxypeptidase-like (SCPL) acyltransferase that transfers (R)-phenyllactate from (R)-phenyllactylglucose onto tropine; KEGG has reassigned R08432 to EC 2.4.1.400 / K25583, superseding the phenyllactyl-CoA hypothesis in the ModelSEED name
organism_context: Atropa belladonna and other tropane-alkaloid Solanaceae (Anisodus, Datura); UGT1 makes the glucose ester acyl donor in a separate step
rationale: Qiu et al. identified UGT1 and LS as the two genes required for littorine biosynthesis, with LS an SCPL acyltransferase; SCPL enzymes retain the alpha/beta-hydrolase fold but have lost peptidase activity and act solely as acyltransferases, so this is one catalytic activity.
direction_note: ModelSEED uses free (R)-phenyllactate (cpd03331 = KEGG C05607) in place of the activated phenyllactylglucose ester, deleting the energy source for the new ester bond (and the released glucose/water), which is exactly what makes the condensation look uphill and drives the spurious '<'.

enzyme_name: Norgalanthamine N-methyltransferase - LaTMT2, a Golgi-localised SAM-dependent methyltransferase of the gamma-tocopherol-methyltransferase family that N-methylates norgalanthamine to galanthamine (and nornarwedine to narwedine)
organism_context: Leucojum aestivum (Amaryllidoideae); homologues in Narcissus and Lycoris
rationale: Lamichhane et al. showed LaTMT2 methylates both nornarwedine and norgalanthamine in vitro, with a single SAM-dependent methyltransferase activity; the tocopherol-methylating activity of the family was retained by the paralogue LaTMT1, not reported for LaTMT2, so no fused second activity.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way toward galanthamine; the equation here is balanced and sound, so ModelSEED's '<' is simply the wrong direction for this methyltransferase.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; salsolinol arises from L-DOPA only after decarboxylation to dopamine (aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, DDC) followed by Pictet-Spengler condensation with acetaldehyde, which is largely non-enzymatic though a stereoselective '(R)-salsolinol synthase' has been proposed and never isolated
organism_context: Mammalian brain and peripheral tissue; also food-derived
rationale: KEGG marks R08443 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction', so no single enzyme catalyses L-DOPA to salsolinol; the condensation half of the route is chiefly spontaneous and the proposed salsolinol synthase remains molecularly unidentified.
direction_note: The acetaldehyde co-substrate, the CO2 of decarboxylation and the condensation water are all absent, so the +39 to +98 kJ/mol behind the '<' call is not this chemistry's free energy; the route only runs toward salsolinol.

enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG states R08463 is the two-step sum of R09088 and R09089, i.e. L-phenylalanine to 1-phenylpropane-1,2-dione and then transamination to (S)-cathinone, with only transcriptome-level candidate genes in khat
organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) phenylpropylamino alkaloid pathway; related chemistry in Ephedra sinica
rationale: KEGG itself decomposes the entry into two reactions, so no single enzyme catalyses it; the khat EST/transcriptome studies by Hagel and Groves list only candidate transaminases and have not confirmed a catalysing protein.
direction_note: Phenylalanine is the pathway entry point and cathinone the product, so the biosynthetic direction is forward; the '<' comes from a +48 to +61 kJ/mol estimate on an equation that omits the pyruvate/CO2 and the amino donor of the two real steps.
